subject: math
title: Measurement Conversions
seo_title: Grade 4 Measurement Conversion Worksheets: Metric, Customary and Time Units with Tables
standard_text: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table. Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 measurement conversion worksheets: km, m, cm, kg, g, L, mL, lb, oz, ft, in, yd, hours, minutes and seconds. Two-column tables, mixed units, comparing and word problems with money. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply.
key_sub: There are more of the small units. 1 ft = 12 in, so 3 ft = 3 × 12 = 36 in. For mixed units, add the leftover: 2 hr 15 min = 120 + 15 = 135 min.
body_html:
Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply

A foot is longer than an inch, so it takes more inches to cover the same length. To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply by how many small units are in 1 big unit.

Feet to inches

3 ft = ☐ in

1 ft = 12 in. Multiply: 3 × 12 = 36.

Answer: 36 in

Conversion facts to know

MeasureFacts
Metric length1 km = 1,000 m   1 m = 100 cm
Metric mass1 kg = 1,000 g
Metric liquid volume1 L = 1,000 mL
Customary length1 yd = 3 ft   1 ft = 12 in
Customary weight1 lb = 16 oz
Time1 hr = 60 min   1 min = 60 sec   1 day = 24 hr   1 week = 7 days

Make a two-column table

Write the big unit on the left and the small unit on the right. Every row uses the same rule: left number × 1,000 = right number.

Mixed units

Change the big unit first, then add the leftover small units.

Hours and minutes

2 hr 15 min = ☐ min

2 × 60 = 120 min. Add the leftover 15 min: 120 + 15 = 135.

Answer: 135 min

To compare two measurements, change both to the same unit. 5 ft = 60 in, so 5 ft is longer than 58 in.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 100 for every unit (1 hr = 100 min)1 hr = 60 min, 1 lb = 16 oz, 1 ft = 12 in
Dividing to get the smaller unit (6 ft = 2 in)Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply (6 ft = 72 in)
Forgetting the leftover (2 ft 5 in = 24 in)Add the leftover inches: 24 + 5 = 29 in
Writing the digits together (4 m 8 cm = 48 cm)4 m = 400 cm, so 4 m 8 cm = 408 cm
Comparing only the numbers (58 in > 5 ft)Use one unit first: 5 ft = 60 in, and 60 > 58

faq.q: How do you convert larger units to smaller units in 4th grade?
faq.a: Multiply by the number of small units in 1 large unit. For example, 1 ft = 12 in, so 4 ft = 4 × 12 = 48 in.

faq.q: What measurement conversions should a 4th grader know?
faq.a: 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 L = 1,000 mL, 1 lb = 16 oz, 1 yd = 3 ft, 1 ft = 12 in, 1 hr = 60 min and 1 min = 60 sec.

faq.q: What is a two-column conversion table?
faq.a: It lists a measurement in a big unit on the left and the same measurement in a small unit on the right, such as 1 ft | 12 in, 2 ft | 24 in, 3 ft | 36 in. Every row follows the same multiplication rule.

It is the Common Core Grade 4 standard for knowing the relative sizes of units and writing a measurement in a smaller unit, such as 3 hr = 180 min. 4.MD.A.2 uses these conversions in word problems about distance, time, volume, mass and money.

items.q: How long does it take to brush your teeth?
items.e: Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes. 2 seconds is far too short, and 2 hours is far too long.

items.q: What is the weight of a loaf of bread?
items.e: A loaf of bread weighs about 1 pound (16 ounces). 1 ounce is about the weight of a slice of bread.

items.q: A classroom door is about how tall?
items.e: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, about 2 meters. 2 cm is shorter than your finger, and 2 km is a long walk.

items.q: How many inches are in 1 foot?
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in. A 12-inch ruler is exactly 1 foot long.

items.q: What is the mass of a pineapple?
items.e: A pineapple has a mass of about 1 kilogram (1,000 g). 1 g is the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: How many feet are in 1 yard?
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. A yardstick is as long as 3 rulers.

items.q: How many meters are in 1 kilometer?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 km = 1,000 m.

items.q: How many ounces are in 1 pound?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz (not 10 or 12).

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest unit of length to the longest?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm and 1 km = 1,000 m, so centimeter < meter < kilometer.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest unit of time to the longest?
items.e: 1 min = 60 sec and 1 hr = 60 min, so second < minute < hour.

items.q: How many seconds are in 1 minute?
items.e: 1 min = 60 sec (not 100).

items.q: You walk for about 15 minutes. About how far do you go?
items.e: In 15 minutes you can walk about 1 kilometer (1,000 m). 1 m is just one big step.

items.q: How many centimeters are in 1 meter?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so 1 m = 100 cm.

items.q: 1 hour is how many times as long as 1 minute?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min (not 100), so 1 hour is 60 times as long as 1 minute.

items.q: How much water does a small water bottle hold?
items.e: A small water bottle holds about 500 milliliters, which is half of 1 liter. 5 mL is just one spoonful.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest unit of length to the longest?
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in and 1 yd = 3 ft, so inch < foot < yard.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 pound = 16 ounces, so a pound is heavier than an ounce. The others are backward: 1 ft = 12 in, 1 kg = 1,000 g, and 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: How many milliliters are in 1 liter?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kg = 1,000 g.

items.q: What is the mass of a paper clip?
items.e: A paper clip is very light. Its mass is about 1 gram. 1 kilogram is about the mass of a pineapple.

items.q: How many minutes are in 9 hours?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger than minutes, so you need more minutes: multiply. 9 × 60 = 540, so 9 hr = 540 min.

items.q: How many days are in 9 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Weeks are bigger than days, so you need more days: multiply. 9 × 7 = 63, so 9 weeks = 63 days.

items.q: Convert. 4 lb = ☐ oz
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger than ounces, so you need more ounces: multiply. 4 × 16 = 64, so 4 lb = 64 oz.

items.q: How many centimeters are in 7 meters?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so you need more centimeters: multiply. 7 × 100 = 700, so 7 m = 700 cm.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 3 × 1,000 = 3,000, so 3 kg = 3,000 g.

items.q: How many inches are in 8 feet?
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger than inches, so you need more inches: multiply. 8 × 12 = 96, so 8 ft = 96 in.

items.q: Convert. 5 yd = ☐ ft
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Yards are bigger than feet, so you need more feet: multiply. 5 × 3 = 15, so 5 yd = 15 ft.

items.q: How many milliliters are in 8 liters?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so you need more milliliters: multiply. 8 × 1,000 = 8,000, so 8 L = 8,000 mL.

items.q: Convert. 6 min = ☐ sec
items.e: 1 min = 60 sec. Minutes are bigger than seconds, so you need more seconds: multiply. 6 × 60 = 360, so 6 min = 360 sec.

items.q: Convert. 7 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so you need more meters: multiply. 7 × 1,000 = 7,000, so 7 km = 7,000 m.

items.q: How many grams are in 30 kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 30 × 1,000 = 30,000, so 30 kg = 30,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 23 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so you need more centimeters: multiply. 23 × 100 = 2,300, so 23 m = 2,300 cm.

items.q: How many ounces are in 11 pounds?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Pounds are bigger than ounces, so you need more ounces: multiply. 11 × 16 = 176, so 11 lb = 176 oz.

items.q: Convert. 11 hr = ☐ min
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min. Hours are bigger than minutes, so you need more minutes: multiply. 11 × 60 = 660, so 11 hr = 660 min.

items.q: How many meters are in 24 kilometers?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so you need more meters: multiply. 24 × 1,000 = 24,000, so 24 km = 24,000 m.

items.q: Convert. 18 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so you need more milliliters: multiply. 18 × 1,000 = 18,000, so 18 L = 18,000 mL.

items.q: Convert. 15 ft = ☐ in
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in. Feet are bigger than inches, so you need more inches: multiply. 15 × 12 = 180, so 15 ft = 180 in.

items.q: How many seconds are in 11 minutes?
items.e: 1 min = 60 sec. Minutes are bigger than seconds, so you need more seconds: multiply. 11 × 60 = 660, so 11 min = 660 sec.

items.q: Convert. 5 days = ☐ hr
items.e: 1 day = 24 hr. Days are bigger than hours, so you need more hours: multiply. 5 × 24 = 120, so 5 days = 120 hr.

items.q: How many feet are in 18 yards?
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Yards are bigger than feet, so you need more feet: multiply. 18 × 3 = 54, so 18 yd = 54 ft.

items.e: 1 min = 60 sec, so every number on the right is the left number × 60. 8 × 60 = 480.

items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so the right number is always the left number × 100. 11 × 100 = 1,100, so 11 m = 1,100 cm fits.

items.e: 1 min = 60 sec. Each left number times 60 gives the right number, for example 2 × 60 = 120. Adding 60 does not work: 2 + 60 = 62, not 120.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft, so every number on the right is the left number × 3. 7 × 3 = 21.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so every number on the right is the left number × 1,000. 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?

items.q: Which rule changes the left column into the right column?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Each left number times 16 gives the right number, for example 6 × 16 = 96. Adding 16 does not work: 6 + 16 = 22, not 96.

items.e: 1 ft = 12 in, so the right number is always the left number × 12. 9 × 12 = 108, so 9 ft = 108 in fits.

items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz, so every number on the right is the left number × 16. 7 × 16 = 112.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz, so every number on the right is the left number × 16. 6 × 16 = 96.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: Each row follows the rule 1 day = 24 hr. Go backward: how many days make 192 hr? 192 ÷ 24 = 8. Check: 8 × 24 = 192.

items.q: Which rule changes the left column into the right column?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Each left number times 1,000 gives the right number, for example 3 × 1,000 = 3,000. Adding 1,000 does not work: 3 + 1,000 = 1,003, not 3,000.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: Each row follows the rule 1 m = 100 cm. Go backward: how many meters make 800 cm? 800 ÷ 100 = 8. Check: 8 × 100 = 800.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in, so every number on the right is the left number × 12. 7 × 12 = 84.

items.q: Which row could be added to this table?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL, so the right number is always the left number × 1,000. 9 × 1,000 = 9,000, so 9 L = 9,000 mL fits.

items.q: Which row could be added to this table?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so the right number is always the left number × 60. 10 × 60 = 600, so 10 hr = 600 min fits.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so every number on the right is the left number × 7. 9 × 7 = 63.

items.q: Which rule changes the left column into the right column?
items.e: 1 yd = 3 ft. Each left number times 3 gives the right number, for example 3 × 3 = 9. Adding 3 does not work: 3 + 3 = 6, not 9.

items.q: What number goes in the ? box?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so every number on the right is the left number × 60. 4 × 60 = 240.

items.q: Convert. 2 L 750 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: Change the liters first: 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 mL. Then add the leftover milliliters: 2,000 + 750 = 2,750 mL.

items.q: Convert. 4 m 8 cm = ☐ cm
items.e: Change the meters first: 4 × 100 = 400 cm. Then add the leftover centimeters: 400 + 8 = 408 cm.

items.q: Convert. 3 hr 20 min = ☐ min
items.e: Change the hours first: 3 × 60 = 180 min. Then add the leftover minutes: 180 + 20 = 200 min.

items.q: Convert. 2 ft 5 in = ☐ in
items.e: Change the feet first: 2 × 12 = 24 in. Then add the leftover inches: 24 + 5 = 29 in.

items.q: Convert. 4 kg 250 g = ☐ g
items.e: Change the kilograms first: 4 × 1,000 = 4,000 g. Then add the leftover grams: 4,000 + 250 = 4,250 g.

items.q: Convert. 2 lb 7 oz = ☐ oz
items.e: Change the pounds first: 2 × 16 = 32 oz. Then add the leftover ounces: 32 + 7 = 39 oz.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: Change the kilograms first: 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 g. Then add the leftover grams: 2,000 + 50 = 2,050 g.

items.q: Convert. 5 km 300 m = ☐ m
items.e: Change the kilometers first: 5 × 1,000 = 5,000 m. Then add the leftover meters: 5,000 + 300 = 5,300 m.

items.q: Convert. 4 min 15 sec = ☐ sec
items.e: Change the minutes first: 4 × 60 = 240 sec. Then add the leftover seconds: 240 + 15 = 255 sec.

items.q: Convert. 3 yd 2 ft = ☐ ft
items.e: Change the yards first: 3 × 3 = 9 ft. Then add the leftover feet: 9 + 2 = 11 ft.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change everything to grams: 2 kg = 2,000 g and 2 kg 75 g = 2,075 g. In order: 2,075 g, 2,070 g, 2,000 g, 1,950 g. So the answer is 2 kg 75 g.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change everything to centimeters: 4 m = 400 cm and 3 m 60 cm = 360 cm. In order: 350 cm, 360 cm, 400 cm, 410 cm. So the answer is 350 cm.

items.q: Which is true?
Which is the longest?
items.e: Change everything to inches: 5 ft = 60 in and 1 yd 1 ft = 3 ft + 1 ft = 48 in. In order: 60 in, 58 in, 55 in, 48 in. So the answer is 5 ft.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz, so 3 lb = 3 × 16 = 48 oz. 2 lb = 32 oz, which is more than 30 oz.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 ft = 12 in, so 4 ft = 4 × 12 = 48 in. 5 ft = 60 in (15 is the number of feet in 5 yards).

items.q: Which is the longest amount of time?
items.e: Change everything to minutes: 2 hr = 120 min (not 200) and 1 hr 50 min = 110 min. In order: 130 min, 120 min, 110 min, 100 min. So the answer is 130 min.

items.q: Which is the lightest?
items.e: Change everything to ounces: 2 lb = 32 oz (not 20) and 1 lb 15 oz = 31 oz. In order: 30 oz, 31 oz, 32 oz, 34 oz. So the answer is 30 oz.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 hr = 60 min, so 3 hr = 180 min, and 180 < 200. 2 hr = 120 min, which is less than 150 min.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change everything to milliliters: 1 L = 1,000 mL and 1 L 50 mL = 1,050 mL. In order: 1,100 mL, 1,050 mL, 1,000 mL, 900 mL. So the answer is 1,100 mL.

sets.title: Word problems with measurements and money

items.q: A movie starts at 6:45 p.m. It is 1 hr 50 min long. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 7:45 p.m. Add 50 minutes: 15 minutes gets to 8:00, then 35 more minutes is 8:35 p.m.

items.q: Jack has a board that is 6 feet long. He cuts it into pieces that are 8 inches long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: 6 ft = 6 × 12 = 72 in. How many 8-inch pieces are in 72 inches? 72 ÷ 8 = 9 pieces.

items.q: A relay race is 2 km long. Four runners each run the same distance. How many meters does each runner run?
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m. Share it equally: 2,000 ÷ 4 = 500 m.

items.q: A 2 L bottle of water costs $1.80. A 500 mL bottle costs $0.65. Mia needs 2 L of water. How much does she save by buying the 2 L bottle instead of 500 mL bottles?
Four friends share the cost of an $18.00 pizza equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: $18.00 ÷ 4. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 with 2 dollars left over. 2 dollars = 200 cents, and 200 ÷ 4 = 50 cents. Each friend pays $4.50 (not $4.20).

items.q: A pitcher holds 3 L of lemonade. How many 500 mL bottles can be filled from the pitcher?
items.e: 3 L = 3,000 mL. How many groups of 500 mL are in 3,000 mL? 3,000 ÷ 500 = 6 bottles.

items.q: A bean plant grows for 3 weeks and 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 3 weeks = 21 days. Add the leftover 4 days: 21 + 4 = 25 days.

items.q: Nora needs 5 yards of ribbon. She has 12 feet of ribbon. How many more feet does she need?
items.e: 5 yd = 5 × 3 = 15 ft. Find the missing part: 15 − 12 = 3 ft.

items.q: Pencils cost 45 cents each. Luis buys 6 pencils. How much does he pay?
items.e: 6 × 45 cents = 270 cents. 100 cents = $1, so 270 cents = $2.70.

items.q: Maya runs 3 km and then walks 450 m. How many meters does she go in all?
Ruby's soccer practice starts at 3:40 p.m. and ends at 5:15 p.m. How long is practice?
items.e: From 3:40 to 4:40 is 1 hour. From 4:40 to 5:00 is 20 minutes, and 5:00 to 5:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hr + 20 min + 15 min = 1 hr 35 min.

items.q: A bag holds 8 apples. Each apple has a mass of 150 g. What is the mass of all the apples?
A recipe needs 1 pound of cheese. Zoe has 10 ounces. How many more ounces does she need?
items.e: 1 lb = 16 oz. Find the missing part: 16 − 10 = 6 oz.

items.q: Owen drinks 3 glasses of milk every day. Each glass holds 250 mL. How much milk does he drink in 1 week?
items.e: One day: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. 1 week = 7 days, so 7 × 750 = 5,250 mL.

items.q: A bag has 2 kg of flour. A baker uses 750 g. How many grams of flour are left?
items.e: Use the same unit: 2 kg = 2,000 g. Then subtract: 2,000 − 750 = 1,250 g.

items.q: A song is 3 minutes 25 seconds long. Kai plays it 2 times. How many seconds is that?
items.e: 3 min = 3 × 60 = 180 sec, so the song is 180 + 25 = 205 seconds. 2 times: 2 × 205 = 410 seconds.

items.q: Lily has a rope that is 3 m long. She cuts off 85 cm. How long is the rope now?
items.e: Use the same unit: 3 m = 300 cm. The rope gets shorter, so subtract: 300 − 85 = 215 cm.

items.q: Ava reads for 12 hour on Monday and 14 hour on Tuesday. How many minutes does she read in all?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30, and one fourth of 60 is 15. In all: 30 + 15 = 45 minutes.

items.q: Sofia has $5.00. She buys a juice for $1.35 and a muffin for $2.40. How much change does she get?
A family drives for 3 hours on Saturday and 2 12 hours on Sunday. How many minutes do they drive in all?
items.e: Saturday: 3 × 60 = 180 min. Sunday: 2 × 60 = 120 min, plus 12 hour = 30 min, so 150 min. In all: 180 + 150 = 330 minutes.
